sections.html: Strophidon sathete is the largest moray eel in the world. It originates from brackish water regions and is euryhaline.
It is rare and relatively expensive in the ornamental fish trade, because it has to be collected by hand and in single specimens. They live very secretively and have to be dug out of the ground.
It inhabits the same habitats (lower reaches of rivers) as the common freshwater moray, Gymnothorax tile.
S. sathete can reach a total length of around 4 metres. The tank must be absolutely safely covered, otherwise the morays will break out.

Like scats or monos, they are completely tolerant of both pure freshwater and pure marine water (euryhaline), but for long-term keeping it is highly recommended to add 10–20 grams of sea salt per litre of water.
They feed on large meaty foods, such as whole fish, pieces of fish, shrimps, etc.

Towards conspecifics this species is very peaceful. However, they try to feed on any other fish that seems to fit their mouth, and the mouth is really large, so it is best to keep them in a one-species tank. In the aquarium they tend to hide a lot at first, but after some time they learn that the keeper means food.
Strophidon: not explained in the original description, but probably from ancient Greek, meaning "with teeth turned backwards". sathete: after the vernacular name of the species in Bengal.
